GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Edit only `cpp/gateway/**` and `static/**`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.


HARD WORKING RULE: your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed. Commit after each merge and each fix; report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-gemini-merge-20261119.md` updated in the same commits. After a restart read the report and `git log` first.

TASK
1. `git fetch origin agent-jobs/cppgw-conformance-pin-20261119-44467964951-1` and merge it (ordinary merge commit; a trial merge shows no conflicts). It brings the port of recent production changes (DeepSeek compaction at 75% of usable context and related) and pins the paired conformance suite to current production.
2. `git fetch origin codex/antigravity-gemini-subscription-20261118` (head must be `8110276d0f374ac64cc4edff32f5a1f02cfe3706`; stop and report if it is not) and merge it with an ordinary merge commit so its ancestry is preserved. It was written by another agent on an OLDER base that still had the TypeScript and Rust trees. It adds a "Gemini subscription" provider: the gateway launches the Antigravity CLI (`agy`) as a child process to serve Gemini models, plus an admin quota view. Expected conflicts and their resolution:
   - `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/provider-decision-journal.md`, `tests/admin-auth-ui.test.ts`, `tests/static-assets.test.ts` (modify/delete): they belong to deleted trees: keep them deleted. After the merge, `git ls-files` must show NO path under `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `rust/`, `docs/`, `ops/`, `lib/`, `tools/` at the repository root and no `.github/workflows/deno-deploy.yml`: remove anything the merge re-added there (git may re-add files silently without a conflict). If the removed `ops/README.md` or docs contained operator instructions for installing and signing in `agy`, make sure `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md` carries them.
   - `cpp/gateway/tools/manifest.py` (modify/delete): this generator was retired by the cleanup; keep it deleted and make sure `cpp/gateway/tools/cmake-sources.py` and `PORT-MANIFEST.json` are consistent with the new Gemini sources (the build must pick up `src/provider/gemini.cpp` and `src/admin/gemini_quota.cpp`) with a meaningful count check, not a loosened one.
   - `cpp/gateway/include/uos/deepseek/waterfall.hpp` and any other file both sides changed for the DeepSeek compaction rule: your branch's version (from step 1, ported from production with tests) wins; drop the Gemini branch's duplicate change.
   - Moved inputs: the cleanup moved `tools/native-kv/` to `cpp/gateway/packaging/native-kv/` and the confinement C source to `cpp/gateway/packaging/confinement/permissions-native.c`. Re-apply any Gemini change to those files at the new location. The C++ confinement (`src/runtime/permissions_linux.cpp`) now does more than that C file: correct every comment or document that calls it a port of it.
3. SECURITY REVIEW ITEMS (a review of this branch was done; most findings were fixed in its last commit: verify each in the code and fix what is not true):
   a. With `UOS_GATEWAY_ENABLE_ANTIGRAVITY` unset or not exactly `1`, the sandbox must be byte-for-byte what it is on your starting branch: same Landlock read/write/execute sets, `execve`/`execveat` and non-thread `clone` denied by seccomp, execute grants rejected. Prove it with a test that compares the computed permissions and filter with and without the Gemini code path present, and keep the existing confinement tests unchanged.
   b. With the flag set: the child process exception is still process-wide (seccomp cannot scope it). Document that plainly in `docs/RUNTIME.md` and `docs/SECURITY-LIMITS.md`. The branch grants execute on `/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`; Landlock checks execute only at `execve`, so `ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 <any readable ELF>` can start other programs from readable locations (`/usr/lib` is readable and the state directory is writable). Determine whether `agy` is statically linked (`file`/`readelf -d` on a real `agy` is not possible on your runner: reason from the branch's notes and its listed library dependencies; it lists shared libraries, so it is dynamic). Since the loader grant is then required, reduce the exposure as far as Landlock allows (grant execute only on the canonical loader path and `agy`; make sure no writable directory is also readable-as-ELF by the child beyond what `agy` needs; consider dropping the gateway's own write grants in the child with a second, stricter Landlock ruleset applied between fork and exec if `rt::process::spawn` allows a pre-exec hook), add a test that a direct `posix_spawn` of another binary is refused and a test documenting what the loader path can still reach, and state the residual risk in one paragraph for the owner.
   c. The child gets an explicit minimal environment (no provider keys, tokens or gateway secrets), verified by a test using a fake `agy` that prints its environment.
   d. A client disconnect kills the child; there is a gateway-side deadline; the child is killed and reaped on every error path including output-limit errors; stdout/stderr readers start before stdin is written. Apply the central limits (`include/uos/rt/limits.hpp`) to CLI output sizes.
   e. A CLI result without token counts must not crash a streamed Responses or Chat request (there was a null dereference of `usage`): test it.
   f. CLI stderr/error text is not returned verbatim to API clients (log it redacted); provider health is not marked failed by client errors (413) or a missing CLI (503).
   g. `src/handler/terminal_route.cpp`: the branch changed a return value for ALL providers for the benefit of a Gemini test: revert it unless existing-provider behaviour is provably unchanged (explain).
   h. Recorded differential vectors must be honest: if a `.inc` file says it was recorded from TypeScript but now contains Gemini rows no TypeScript produced, say so in its header instead.
   i. The new code must follow this branch's coroutine lifetime rules (the branch predates a lifetime audit): no owning temporaries or structured bindings in a `co_await` full-expression, coroutine lambdas own their captures, abort listeners unregistered on every path.
4. Verification on the merged tree: `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py --check`; all four release shards and all four sanitizer shards (state binaries and cases; expect about 455 binaries); the paired conformance gate as `cpp/gateway/conformance/README.md` documents (only the two known shared failures); `git ls-files | grep -E '\.(ts|rs)$'` lists only the tooling files your starting branch and step 1 already have.
